raw:
Bea is not in the building at lunchtime. Nell brings a wrapped sandwich out from the office, while Jo occupies one end of the joined tables with a bowl of reheated chickpea stew, black coffee and a spread of supplier invoices.

You sit with your lunch at the clear end.

Jo has weighted the papers with a sugar jar. Several prices are circled in pencil.

“The cheese quote came in,” she tells Nell. “I can keep the pie on the opening menu, but the price per slice needs to go up twenty pence.”

“If that’s what it costs, charge it.”

“That’s what it costs today. I’m ringing them again at two before I print anything.”

Nell takes another bite of her sandwich. “Send me the final version when you’re satisfied. I’ll update the website from that.”

Jo makes a note beside the circled figure. “Tea can stay where it is. Coffee too. I’m not changing three prices because one supplier’s having a difficult month.”

They move on to delivery times and the limited refrigerator space behind the counter. Jo knows exactly how many pie dishes will fit without blocking the shelf she needs for milk. Nell records only the agreed delivery window, leaving the quantities to her.

For several minutes, the three of you eat without conversation. Rainwater trails down the front glazing, blurring the buildings opposite.

When Jo finishes, she gathers her invoices for the supplier call. Nell folds her sandwich wrapper and stands.

“I’ll look through the items you flagged in the yellow tray after lunch,” she says. “Take the rest of your break before you start again.”

Jo returns to the kitchen, and Nell goes back into the office. Neither turns the meal into another task for you.
reasoning_summaries: **Planning natural lunch dialogue with Jo and Nell**
